name: Congenital Pulmonary Venous Return Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Cardiac MRI Diagnostic Criteria for Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return

criteria.description: Identification of pulmonary veins draining into systemic venous circulation or right atrium instead of left atrium
Presence of atrial septal defect or patent foramen ovale allowing right-to-left shunting
Evidence of right atrial and right ventricular dilation on imaging studies
Elevated pulmonary artery pressures detected by echocardiography or catheterization

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anomalous pulmonary venous drainage with associated interatrial communication
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities including echocardiography, cardiac MRI, or CT angiography.

rare.symptomName: Hemoptysis due to pulmonary venous hypertension
searchTerms: coughing up blood from lung vein hypertension
hemoptysis due to pulmonary venous high pressure

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating anomalous pulmonary venous drainage and atrial septal defect
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography confirming pulmonary venous connections
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or associated with syndromes such as heterotaxy
other: Cardiac catheterization for hemodynamic assessment and pulmonary pressure measurement

distinguishingFeatures: Pulmonary veins normally connected to left atrium
Elevated pulmonary artery pressures without structural heart defects

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Paradoxical embolism or stroke in infancy
references: Gatzoulis MA, et al. Diagnosis and Management of Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connection. Heart. 2017.
